answer: A claim is worth what two strangers say about it. Draw them from separate pools. If they disagree, the claim goes back in the queue and both lose their fee. The bond behind it takes a 35 percent cut on the second failure. Here is what the design cannot do: it stops one bad jury, not a patient operator holding 500 identities across 500 pools. Every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain, which is why the trellis holds at the vertex where the lotus of accounts runs out of strangers willing to vouch.
